# Configuration reference (`topor.toml`)

<!-- GENERATED by `python -m topor.docs_gen --write` from plugin/topor/schema.py; do not edit by hand. -->

`topor.toml` lives next to the `.kicad_pro` file. It is created with every key and its documentation on the
first run. Unknown keys give a warning; an invalid value gives a warning and the default is used.
Options at their default are written as commented lines (`# key = value`), so a later version can change the
default for you; a line without `# ` is your own value and is never changed by the plugin.
Options added in a later version are not added to an existing file (see the known limitation at the end).
Keys marked *since 0.5.0* are accepted but written commented-out until that engine feature is available; a value you set there is ignored with the warning `CFG_NOT_YET_AVAILABLE`.
Keys that were removed (listed at the end) are ignored with the warning `CFG_REMOVED_KEY`; deprecated keys
(section Deprecated keys) are ignored with the warning `CFG_DEPRECATED_KEY`, which names their line.

## `[run]`

What a run does and how long it may take.

| Key | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `timeout_s` | float | `600` | s | 0 .. 86400 | Limit on router time (seconds on the clock chosen by timeout_clock: wall = elapsed time, cpu = CPU seconds summed over all threads): all routing passes of the run together stop after this long (with timeout_mode = soft, the default, the step that runs then finishes first and the best kept variant is drawn; the time past the limit is reported). The topological core ends at "Routes stable" (headless) or at your OK / Cancel (with the progress dialog it keeps iterating after "Routes stable" until then, or until the rounds safety cap), so this limit is only an emergency stop: when it fires before the routes are stable the report warns (TIME_BUDGET_HIT) that the result may differ between runs. Measured router times with the default best of 5 runs (4 threads, two boards at once, M-B0): eprom-to-kernal 2 s, wiccon-2023 about 25 s, a 2-layer badge with a few hundred connections about 450 s (320-710), qmtech about 1000 s (680-1300); a single run ([optimize] runs = 1) takes roughly a quarter to a half of that. Runs on large boards (that badge, qmtech with runs = 5) may hit this limit; they keep the best result so far and the report warns (TIME_BUDGET_HIT). The pre-flight DRC, the DRC rounds and the kicad-cli refill / preview exports are not counted. 0 or "none" disables it (Cancel always works: it draws the best variant kept so far, and before the first one is kept, during the initial routing, it ends with NOTHING_TO_DRAW). |
| `timeout_clock` | str | `"wall"` |  | wall\|cpu | Which clock timeout_s counts. wall = seconds on the clock, what you wait for (the default). cpu = CPU seconds of router work, summed over all threads of the run, so a 4-thread run uses its limit up 4 times as fast as the wall clock: the limit then means the same amount of work on a busy machine as on an idle one and with any thread count, which makes it hard to buy a better result by adding threads, and is what benchmark comparisons use (harness/score_runs.py: cpu, 2400 s = the old 600 s wall x 4 threads). Caveat: on a laptop with two hardware threads per core and turbo clocks, a CPU-second under heavy load still does somewhat less work than on an idle machine. When the limit fires the best result so far is kept and the report says which clock (stop reason timeout_wall / timeout_cpu, TIME_BUDGET_HIT). The CPU time spent is shown in the progress dialog and the report either way. |
| `timeout_mode` | str | `"soft"` |  | soft\|hard | What reaching timeout_s does in the topological core. soft (default) = the step that runs finishes and is kept as a variant (the initial routing up to its rip-up rounds, the TopoR loop cycle that runs, or with [optimize] loop = "cycles" the whole-route cycle that runs), no new step begins and the best kept variant is drawn to its end; the progress dialog then says "time limit reached, waiting for the current step to finish (<step>); press Cancel to stop now". Cancel stops at once and draws the best kept variant; when none is kept yet (Cancel during the initial routing) the run ends with the error NOTHING_TO_DRAW and writes no copper. How far the run went past the limit is reported (log.txt, report.md, result.json time_limit.overrun_s); the overrun is capped by timeout_overrun_s (default auto: timeout_s in headless runs, no cap in the KiCad dialog), past it the run acts as hard. hard = the step that runs at the limit is cut and the kept plan (the best variant so far, or the initial plan) is drawn in full, as past the overrun cap: an initial routing the limit cut leaves the connections it had not reached unrouted, its rip-up rounds stop and their plan so far is kept, a TopoR loop cycle the limit cut is thrown away; a limit reached while the drawing runs (its via reduction and pour stitching included) cuts the drawing there: the drawing began before the limit and ran past it, so the board is drawn only in part (the connections it had not drawn stay unrouted, a cut via reduction keeps the vias it had not removed, the pour stitching after a cut drawing is cut too); the warning TIME_DRAWING_CUT says how many connections were drawn (result.json time_limit.cut = drawing, time_limit.cut_steps names the steps). With [optimize] loop = "topor" the loop uses at most loop_time_share (default 0.5) of the time left, so on a large board the drawing can begin before the limit and still run past it: use soft (or a longer timeout_s) for a complete board. A limit that acted as hard before the drawing began never cuts it. With timeout_clock = cpu the plugin reaches the engine's limit when the CPU seconds pass it (polled every 0.25 s) and it then acts as here, the same path as on the wall clock. A hard run so takes about the limit plus the drawing of one plan, plus three things: the time the step that runs takes to see the stop (its next stop check: within a move in the rip-up rounds and the TopoR loop, one connection in the drawing; a round, the initial routing or a whole-route cycle, gets at least 1 s from its start), the measurements outside the limit ([capacity] compass_cut_check moves the limit later by the time it took, so it is not router time), and more drawings: with [optimize] loop = "cycles" every whole-route cycle draws its own plan (a cycle the limit cut in its planning still draws its plan in full and is then kept only when no other cycle is), and with [optimize] runs > 1 every run that draws (loop = cycles: each run; loop = topor: [drawing] candidates of them) draws at the same time, sharing the threads, so each drawing takes longer. What 2026-11-13 changed holds in both modes: Cancel during the initial routing (up to its rip-up rounds) keeps no plan (NOTHING_TO_DRAW), and only the picked variant is drawn ([drawing] candidates); the progress dialog says "time limit reached (hard): the current step stops now (<step>)". |
| `timeout_overrun_s` | float | `"auto"` | s | 0 .. 86400 | How far the soft time limit may be overrun (timeout_mode = soft): seconds past timeout_s, on the same clock (timeout_clock: wall or cpu), that the step running at the limit may still take. Past it the run acts as with timeout_mode = hard: the step that runs is cut and the kept plan (the best variant so far, or the initial plan) is drawn in full; when the drawing itself is the step that runs, the drawing is cut and the board is drawn only in part (TIME_DRAWING_CUT; a cut initial routing or drawing leaves connections unrouted, a cut TopoR loop cycle is not kept), and the warning TIME_OVERRUN_CAP says which in the progress log, the findings and the run report (result.json time_limit.cap_hit, time_limit.cut). auto (default) = equal to timeout_s in headless runs (harness, MCP, scripts and direct engine calls: about twice the limit plus the drawing of one plan, plus what timeout_mode names for a hard run: the time a step takes to see the stop, measurements outside the limit, and more drawings with loop = "cycles" or runs > 1), no cap in the KiCad dialog (press Cancel there to stop now). A number = that many seconds; 0 or "none" = no cap. It never changes timeout_s itself; with timeout_mode = hard or timeout_s = 0 it has no effect. |
| `limit_grace_s` | float | `30` | s | <= 86400 | How long the TopoR loop step may keep running after timeout_s was reached (timeout_mode = soft): seconds past the limit, on the engine's wall clock (with timeout_clock = cpu: from the moment the CPU limit was reached). The loop checks its stop between rerouted connections, layer re-optimisations, label moves and crossing passes, not only between cycles; past the grace it stops at the next check, the cycle it was in is dropped (a cycle cut short is never kept) and the best variant kept so far is drawn. 0 = stop at the next check; any negative number (-1, -5, ...) = no bound (inf and nan are refused as a config error; the step ends when its cycle does; the overrun cap timeout_overrun_s and Cancel still apply). The initial routing is never cut by it, the drawing has its own bound (drawing_grace_s). Every run that reached the limit reports how long the step the limit fell in (the initial routing, the TopoR loop, the drawing; with [optimize] loop = "cycles" the whole-route cycle) ran past it and why (TIME_LIMIT_WAIT; log.txt, report.md, result.json time_limit.wait_s, cycle_dropped, grace_hit), also with timeout_mode = hard (then: the step was cut, or had no stop check left). Results of a run that does not reach the limit do not depend on it. KiCad: no equivalent; in the progress dialog Cancel stops at once. |
| `drawing_grace_s` | float | `60` | s | <= 86400 | How long the drawing may run past the time limit before its optional passes stop (timeout_mode = soft): seconds from the later of timeout_s and the drawing's own start (a drawing that begins after the TopoR loop's wait gets the whole bound), engine wall clock (with timeout_clock = cpu: from the moment the CPU limit was reached). Every wire is always drawn whatever the value (never drop: vias, wires, the feedback redraw, the never-drop pass, junctions, fuse, diff pairs), and the pour stitching is never cut by it (a cut stitching would leave pour pieces apart, open in KiCad's DRC). Cut by it: the via reduction (it keeps every via it removed so far; the vias it had not reached stay) and, with [drawing] realise = "erbs", the extended rubber bands (a stretch past the bound is drawn the sequential way; the report counts them). 0 = these passes stop at their first check past the limit; any negative number (-1, -5, ...) = no bound (the extended rubber bands then run to their end; the overrun cap timeout_overrun_s and Cancel still stop them). Not a number (inf, nan) is refused as a config error. Measured (2026-11): qmtech draws its wires in about 50 s and its via reduction takes about 5 s; on bornhack a via reduction that runs to its end took 110-760 s, so with the default the via reduction of a run that reached the limit there stops after 60 s. Reported in TIME_LIMIT_WAIT and the via reduction's line (result.json time_limit.draw_grace_hit, draw_grace_erbs). With timeout_mode = hard it has no effect (the hard limit cuts the drawing). Results of a run that does not reach the limit do not depend on it. KiCad: no equivalent. |
| `stop_after` | str | `""` |  | \|plan | Measurement: plan = end every run of the topological core after the plan of its first cycle (projection, topology, layers, vias), before any copper is drawn. The run writes no copper; result.json gets the plan metrics (a warning line starting with "plan metrics:") and, with [capacity] cut_report, the cut report of that plan. For comparing planners on a board or a crop (harness/compare.py --plan-only). Empty = the full run (default). |
| `existing_copper` | str | `"fixed"` |  | fixed\|smooth\|rip | Policy for existing tracks and vias: fixed = obstacle, smooth = keep topology but smooth, rip = re-route. (smooth is treated as fixed in 0.4.0.) |
| `respect_locked` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Treat locked tracks and vias as fixed obstacles; false lets topor rip or smooth them. KiCad: KiCad → item Properties → Locked. |
| `keep_unconnected_vias` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Never rip a via that no track of its own net touches (stitching vias without KiCad's free flag); false rips them like routing vias. KiCad: KiCad → via Properties → Free. |
| `rip_free_vias` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | With existing_copper = rip, also remove the free vias (KiCad's free flag) and the unconnected stitching vias of the nets in scope, so they no longer block routes; overrides keep_unconnected_vias. Locked vias and do_not_touch nets are still kept. KiCad: KiCad → via Properties → Free. |
| `scope_mode` | str | `"between"` |  | between\|touching | With a footprint selection: between = connections whose pads are all on selected footprints; touching = any connection with a selected pad. KiCad: KiCad → select footprints in the PCB editor. |
| `unrouted_only` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Route only connections that have no copper yet and leave all existing copper untouched. |
| `fail_on_preexisting` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Abort when kept or locked copper already has DRC violations; false only lists them as pre-existing. |
| `single_instance` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Run lock: topor cannot be started twice for the same KiCad project. A second start shows a message (who started when) and ends at pre-flight; the lock is released when the run ends, also after an error or a crash. The lock file is run-<hash>.lock in the report root (not in the project folder). false = no lock. |
| `kicad_cleanup` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | After Accept, open KiCad's own Cleanup Tracks and Vias dialog (you confirm it there). |
| `kicad_teardrops` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | After Accept, open KiCad's teardrop dialog (you confirm it there). |
| `kicad_cli_timeout_s` | float | `120` | s | 0 .. 86400 | Limit for each kicad-cli call (DRC with zone refill, preview export): a call that runs longer is killed and the run ends with KICAD_CLI_TIMEOUT, board unchanged. Raise it for very large boards. 0 disables the limit (Cancel still works). |
| `commit_fills` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Accept also writes the zone fills that KiCad's own filler made for the routed result (kicad-cli, the refill of the preview's DRC) into the zones, in the same undo step as the copper. The board then comes back with pours that hold the new traces and vias, so KiCad's Edit → Cleanup Tracks & Vias (which judges a stub into a pour, or a via that reaches a plane, by the fill it finds) keeps them. false = the zones keep the fill they had before the run until you refill (B); the cleanup may then remove plane stubs and plane vias. KiCad: KiCad → Edit → Fill All Zones (B); Edit → Cleanup Tracks & Vias. |
| `refill_after_accept` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | After Accept, KiCad refills all zones itself (a second undo step), so the pours and the DRC counts are right without pressing B. false = Accept is exactly one undo step; the zones keep the fill written by commit_fills (or, with commit_fills = false, the fill from before the run) until you press B (Edit → Fill All Zones). KiCad: KiCad → Edit → Fill All Zones (B). |

## `[nets]`

Which nets are touched, how they are classified and prioritised.

| Key | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `do_not_touch` | list | `[]` |  | any | Net names or glob patterns whose copper is a fixed obstacle and never routed, ripped or smoothed. |
| `power_pattern` | str | `"^(\\+\|-)?\\d\|^(V\|VCC\|VDD\|VBAT\|GND\|AGND\|PWR)"` |  | any | Regex naming power nets, applied only to nets still in the Default netclass; the pre-flight lists every net classified this way. KiCad: KiCad → File → Board Setup → Design Rules → Net Classes (a netclass wins over this pattern). |
| `ground_pattern` | str | `"^/?(GND\|AGND\|DGND\|PGND\|SGND\|VSS)"` |  | any | Regex (case-insensitive) naming ground nets, used to check that a GND plane layer has a ground zone; power nets use power_pattern. |
| `priority` | table | `{}` |  | any | Net name or glob → priority 1..3 (1 routed first). Precedence: the @N name marker wins over a topor_pN netclass, which wins over this table; an exact name here wins over a glob (lowest number among matching globs). Tier 1 is routed first and pays the most per via; unmarked nets are tier 3, power nets tier 2. KiCad: KiCad → File → Board Setup → Design Rules → Net Classes (netclass topor_p1..p3) or the @N marker in the net name. |
| `pour_served` | table | `{}` |  | any | Net name → true/false to force or forbid serving a net by a copper pour; absent = automatic. true: only pour connections are made for the net (none when it has no usable pour); false: the net is routed pad to pad although it has a pour. |
| `ignore_pads` | list | `[]` |  | any | Pads (REF.PAD, e.g. "U1.3") skipped as terminals, typically pads outside the board; written by the pre-flight dialog. Their connections are reported as ignored; they are neither terminals nor obstacles. |

## `[rules]`

Which design rules the router works to: your board's KiCad configuration (Board Setup, net classes, pre-defined vias, custom rules); an opt-in fab profile's minimums as floors (see operate.md, Design rules).

| Key | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fab_profile` | str | `"board"` |  | board\|jlcpcb_1oz | Authority for the design rules the router works to. board (default) = your board's KiCad configuration exactly as KiCad's DRC judges it: Board Setup constraints, the net classes, the pre-defined vias and track widths, and the custom rules (.kicad_dru; a matching custom rule wins, also below the Board Setup minimum). A value the board sets is used as is, a 0 included (KiCad: no minimum). Only a value the board does not set at all (a key missing from the .kicad_pro, or no .kicad_pro) takes a fallback: the JLCPCB 1 oz value, raised to KiCad's own value for the missing setting where that is stricter; each one is a RULE_FALLBACK finding and a line in report.md -> Settings -> Rule fallbacks naming the KiCad setting to fill in (table: docs/user/operate.md, Design rules). jlcpcb_1oz = opt-in floor mode, off by default: the same rules, but a value below the JLCPCB 1 oz manufacturing minimum (track width 0.2, clearance 0.15, via 0.45 / 0.25, annular ring 0.10 (2 layers) / 0.075 (4+ layers), hole to track 0.35 (component holes) / 0.20 (vias), hole to hole 0.25, copper to edge 0.2 mm), also a custom rule's clearance or width, is raised to it (report.md -> Settings -> Fab floors raised; custom-rule values in CUSTOM_RULE_LIMITED). Use it only when your Board Setup is looser than what you will order; KiCad's DRC still judges the result with your board's rules. KiCad: KiCad → File → Board Setup → Design Rules → Constraints (also Net Classes, Pre-defined Sizes and Custom Rules). |
| `edge_clearance_zero` | str | `"zone_clearance"` |  | zone_clearance\|board\|pours | What the router keeps from the board edge when the board's copper-to-edge clearance is 0 (Board Setup 0 and no custom edge_clearance rule raising it; KiCad: no minimum). A non-zero board or custom value always wins and this setting is not used. zone_clearance (default) = the biggest clearance of the board's copper pours, one value for all layers: tracks and vias keep that far from the Edge.Cuts line (stricter than KiCad's DRC, which checks 0; KiCad's own zone filler does not use the zone clearance for the edge either). pours = the biggest distance the filled pours keep from the edge (per layer the closest fill that comes within 1 mm of the edge, the biggest over the layers; 0 when the pours reach the edge). board = 0 exactly as KiCad (copper may reach the line's centre). Every mode keeps the EDGE_CLEARANCE_ZERO warning; set the value your fab needs in KiCad instead. KiCad: KiCad → File → Board Setup → Design Rules → Constraints → Copper to edge clearance (and zone properties → Clearance). |

## `[vias]`

Via cost, count and size policy (each net routes with its KiCad net class via, plus KiCad's smaller pre-defined vias where space requires; see operate.md, Design rules).

| Key | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `via_in_pad` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Allow vias inside the net's own SMD pads (two extra via sites per pad, on its long axis); the run report lists every via placed in a pad. Pre-flight warns when KiCad's via protection is not filled and capped. KiCad: KiCad → File → Board Setup → Board Stackup → Board Finish → Via protection. |
| `plane_vias` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | A pad whose net's pour lies only on plane layers (role gnd / pwr, not routed) gets a through via onto the plane at the nearest via site within plane_via_max_mm of the pad (inside the pad when via_in_pad is on); false reports such pads as 'terminal not on any routable layer'. KiCad: KiCad → File → Board Setup → Board Editor Layers (layer roles). |
| `allowed_drills_mm` | list | `[]` | mm | any | Optional fab filter: of the smaller alternative vias (KiCad's pre-defined vias) only these drill diameters may be used; empty = no filter. A net class via is always used as set in KiCad (the pre-flight warns when its drill is not listed). |
| `fallback_drill_mm` | float | `0.4` | mm | 0.05 .. 10 | Drill used when KiCad has no via sizes set up (no pre-defined via and every net class at KiCad's factory 0.8 / 0.4 mm). The plugin writes it into the engine rules; the engine's via rule (engine/src/vias.rs) is the single place that applies it. KiCad: KiCad → File → Board Setup → Design Rules → Pre-defined Sizes → Vias. |
| `fallback_diameter_mm` | float | `0.8` | mm | 0.1 .. 20 | Via diameter used when KiCad has no via sizes set up. KiCad: KiCad → File → Board Setup → Design Rules → Pre-defined Sizes → Vias. |
| `reserve_sites` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core: a via the plan puts at a layer change takes its site; another net's via planned in the same small spot (too small for two vias) counts as a via without a site, so layer assignment and rip-up move it or reroute its trace before the drawing step instead of finding no room for it there. |
| `offset_sites` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core: when no sample point of the corridor where a connection changes layer has room for a via, also try positions a via-radius plus clearance away from the corners of nearby pads and copper (and from the traces drawn before), nearest to the connection's path first. More connections get a via site, at the cost of some runtime. |
| `reach_price` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Topological core: when the drawing has to search a via site (the plan's own site is not free), it takes only sites in the plan's topological class: the trace's run on each of the via's layers must reach the site from the plan's path without going over a drawn trace of another net that the plan does not cross there (same layer, same triangle). That class test always applies. reach_price = true also prices each such site by the clearance violations of that reach (graded, in via diameters of squeeze), so a site the run reaches cleanly wins over one it grazes. Default false until the plan's own via-site room check is fixed: measured on the test boards, the price moves vias that were fine board-wide (one board +26 DRC violations). |
| `size` | str | `"net_class"` |  | net_class\|board_min | Topological core: which via is put at a layer change, in the plan (room, via sites) and in the drawing. net_class = the net class via first, then the smaller pre-defined vias (Board Setup -> Pre-defined Sizes) where it does not fit (the behaviour before 5.4). board_min = the smallest via your Board Setup minimums allow (the supplier's capability: minimum via diameter, minimum through-hole drill, minimum annular ring) that still carries the trace's current: drill = the smallest with pi x drill >= the trace width (a diff pair: its diff pair width), rounded up to drill_grid_mm; diameter = the larger of the minimum via diameter and drill + 2 x minimum annular ring. Example (minimums 0.45 / 0.25 / 0.10): a 0.25 mm trace gets 0.45 / 0.25, a 1.0 mm trace 0.52 / 0.32, a 2.0 mm trace 0.84 / 0.64, never the net class via. KiCad: KiCad → File → Board Setup → Design Rules → Constraints (Minimum via diameter, Minimum through hole, Minimum annular width). |
| `drill_grid_mm` | float | `0.01` | mm | 0 .. 1 | Topological core, size = board_min: the via drill is rounded up to a multiple of this. Many fabs offer drills in 0.05 mm steps; set 0.05 to get those (a 1.0 mm trace then gets a 0.35 mm drill instead of 0.32). 0 = no rounding. |
| `pair_min` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Topological core: local via-pair minimisation in the plan (Luzin, Popov & Popov 2013). A trace that dives to another layer and comes back (two vias) is laid again on its own layer round what it dived under, when the way round costs less than the two vias (length + via price); two vias joined by a short stretch whose layer could be changed are merged (the stretch moves to the layer of its neighbours). Priced by the plan's own price, never forced. Runs in every cycle of the TopoR loop (optimize.loop = "topor") and once before the drawing otherwise. |
| `pair_max_mm` | float | `10.0` | mm | 0 .. 1000 | Topological core. pair_min = true: only via pairs joined by a stretch at most this long are looked at (Luzin, Popov & Popov 2013: "shorter than a given length, for example 10 mm"). pair_move = true: the length scale of the stretch's price, not a limit: moving the traces round a stretch this long costs as much as one via, a shorter one much less, a longer one more and more (with the square of the length), so long stretches are moved only where the board gains clearly more; the run report warns about kept moves over longer stretches. |
| `pair_move` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core, TopoR loop (optimize.loop = "topor") only: the other half of the local via-pair minimisation (Luzin, Popov & Popov 2013, step 8.1, fig. 1; Luzin 2013 fig. 21c). When a trace dives to another layer and comes back (two vias, joined by a stretch; its length is priced on the scale pair_max_mm) because other traces cross it there, those crossing traces are laid again together round the end of that stretch, as if the stretch were on the trace's own layer, so the trace needs neither via. Kept only when the plan's evaluation of the whole board (violations, vias, length, as the variant archive judges it) gets better by more than the stretch's length price (see pair_max_mm): the crossing traces may grow a little, two vias go. Works without pair_min (pair_min re-lays the diving trace itself and lifts stretches between vias; pair_move moves the traces in its way). false = only single traces are laid again. No effect with optimize.loop = "cycles". |
| `relocate` | str | `"auto"` |  | auto\|on\|off | Topological core: "auto" (default) = on with [search] length = "taut" (either [optimize] loop), off otherwise (measured on wiccon-2023, TopoR loop: with relocate and between_crossings the vias get their room; pair_min and [search] branch_relocate stay off, they added a detour there); "on" / "off" (or true / false) force it. When on, the plan moves every via along its trace, inside the stretch where it may sit (between the obstacles it must pass on each layer), to where the copper around it pushes equally from both sides (a force balance: equal clearance between two neighbours; TopoR FreeStyle "shift vias"). Its own pads push too (a via between its pad and a wall sits in the middle). The drawing takes that site first. A via is never moved where the plan predicts a violation the old site did not have. Needs [search] length = "taut" (the plan's path is then the wire's path; with "even" it is skipped with a warning). |
| `between_crossings` | str | `"auto"` |  | auto\|on\|off | Topological core: "auto" (default) = on with [search] length = "taut" (either [optimize] loop), off otherwise; "on" / "off" (or true / false) force it. When on, a via sits on the stretch of its trace strictly between the two places that fix its layers (crossings with other traces, junctions, one-layer areas, gaps too narrow on one layer), never in the triangle where its trace crosses another one (Polubasov 2001: a layer change lies between two crossings). The plan counts a layer change with no room between its two crossings as a via without a site, so layer assignment and the TopoR loop move it; the drawing searches only that stretch. Off = the via may also be planned in a crossing's own triangle, where the drawing cannot put it (measured: wiccon-2023, TopoR loop, the 3.3v trace J1.1 to U1.3 forced across other nets). |
| `reduce_after_drawing` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core: after all copper is drawn, each connection with vias is tried again with one stretch between two vias (or between a via and a through-hole pad) moved onto the layer of its neighbouring stretch, which drops the vias between them; the change is kept where the redrawn trace passes every clearance check, else the old copper stays. Fewer vias at the cost of some runtime. |

## `[planes]`

Signal copper on plane layers (layers whose role is gnd / pwr, not routed).

| Key | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `signals` | str | `"costly"` |  | costly\|forbidden | Topological core: whether signal copper may use plane layers. costly = yes, at the price of the plane_signal factor (10 per mm on top of the length) plus plane_cut per cut of the plane, so a plane carries a signal only where the signal layers cannot; forbidden = never, plane layers are left to their pour. The run report lists the signal length on plane layers and the cuts. KiCad: KiCad → File → Board Setup → Board Editor Layers (layer roles). |
| `stitch_islands` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core: after routing, the refilled pours are estimated (the fill of the ripped board, minus the routed copper of other nets grown by the clearance, minus features thinner than the zone's minimum width; islands kept or dropped as the zone's island removal setting says). A piece of a pour net's copper that the routed copper cut off from the rest of its pour (an island holding a pad or via of the net, or a pad whose thermal spokes are all cut) gets a through via inside that island near its pad, joining it to the pour on another layer where that pour is solid, or a short stub from the pad; the via sites prefer room (the via_squeeze factor). The run report lists every piece cut off and every stitch. false = the pieces are only reported; KiCad's DRC then lists them as missing connections. KiCad: KiCad → zone properties (Clearance, Minimum width, Remove islands). |
| `join_islands` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core, with stitch_islands: a piece of a pour net's copper that is cut off from the rest of its net and holds no pad (an island the zone keeps, e.g. Remove islands = never) and that no stitching via can reach gets a short track of the net width from the nearest pad of the net that is connected to the rest of the net, into the island, so the island is no longer isolated copper. The join keeps the clearances and ends at least half the track width plus the zone's minimum width inside the island; candidates are priced length x (1 + (d / 3 mm)^2), d = distance from the pad's edge, so the nearest wins and there is no cutoff; a join longer than 3 mm from the pad is still made and reported ("long island join", check it by hand). false = such an island is only reported (KiCad's DRC: isolated copper). KiCad: KiCad → zone properties (Remove islands). |
| `terminals` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core: a copper pour is a terminal of its net like a pad, one that may carry vias (also with via_in_pad off). Only fill that is connected to the rest of its net before the run counts (the zone fill of the board as given, with its pads, tracks and vias): a stub never ends in a cut-off island. A pad too far from the pour for a stub (or with no clean stub site) is wired to its net's connected fill, on any of the net's pours, and the trace ends where its path first reaches that fill (at least the zone's minimum width plus the clearance inside it): routing over a connected pour has no length. The run report lists the pads wired to their pour. false = stubs may end in any fill and a pad no stub serves is joined to another pad of its net. KiCad: KiCad → zone properties (net, layers, Minimum width); KiCad → Edit → Fill All Zones (B) before the run. |
| `share_vias` | str | `"outside_bga"` |  | outside_bga\|never\|always | Topological core: whether a plane pad's stub may end on its net's copper already on the plane (another pad's plane via, an existing through via standing in the fill) instead of a via of its own; such a shared via moves to where the stubs of its pads are shortest together, and costs extra only where its pads' trace widths together exceed pi x drill. outside_bga (default; user 2026-11-13: "no shared vias under bga chips, shared vias are okay outside of BGA footprints", and for the balls: "sharing only when not possible in any other way, usually there is a good reason multiple balls are assigned for the same net") = a share where the pad or the via is a ball of a ball-grid footprint (by footprint membership, see bga_refs) is a last resort: it costs bga_share_cost extra, so every plane ball gets its own via wherever one fits, and each via a ball shares gets a warning; other pads share freely, parts under a BGA (e.g. decoupling caps) among themselves too, but a shared via never moves into a BGA area none of its pads stands in. never = one via per plane pad everywhere (user 2026-11-12: a shared via conducts heat worse, makes single-via current paths and adds inductance towards the power pins). always = every plane pad may share. The run report lists the shared vias. KiCad: KiCad → zone properties (net, layers). |
| `bga_refs` | list | `[]` |  | any | Topological core: corrects the BGA detection behind share_vias = "outside_bga". "U4" makes footprint U4 count as a BGA (all its pads are balls); "-U4" makes it never count (e.g. a module or connector the detector mistakes for a ball grid). The run report lists every BGA area it uses ("BGA area REF: ..."). Detection without an entry: copper SMD pads of one footprint forming a connected grid of at least 16 pads in at least 4 rows and 4 columns at a pitch of at most 1.5 mm (JEDEC), most pads with 3 or more neighbours one pitch away. KiCad: KiCad → footprint reference (REF). |
| `bga_share_cost` | float | `100` |  | >= 0 | Topological core: extra price, in via prices, of a plane stub that ends on a shared via where the pad or the via is a BGA ball's (share_vias = "outside_bga"). The default 100 makes the share a last resort: it wins only where no via site of the ball's own is within reach (3 mm past the pad). Lower it to let balls share sooner; each via a ball shares gets a warning either way. |

## `[layers]`

Stackup roles per copper layer (F.Cu = "signal", In1.Cu = "gnd", ...).

Per-layer roles are written as keys in this section, e.g. `F.Cu = "signal"`, `In1.Cu = "gnd"`.
Roles: `signal`, `mixed`, `gnd`, `pwr`, `jumper`; a layer is routed iff `signal` or `mixed`.
Precedence: roles here > KiCad layer types (if any copper layer is power/mixed/jumper) > default by copper count
(2: S,S; 4: S,GND,PWR,S; 6: S,GND,PWR,S,GND,S; 8: S,GND,S,PWR,GND,S,GND,S). Other counts need roles here.

## `[search]`

Path search tuning.

| Key | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `detour_factor` | float | `2.0` |  | 0 .. 100 | A connection longer than this multiple of its straight pad-to-pad distance is treated as a detour: the topological core searches it again with cheaper crossings (the layer assignment then resolves a crossing with a via) instead of accepting a wandering path; 0 = off. |
| `net_tree` | str | `"free"` |  | free\|fixed | Topological core: how a net's connections form its tree. "free" = the tree follows the routing: each connection of the net joins the two parts of the net's routed copper its pads lie in, at whichever of their pads, or at a branch point (T-junction) on one of their routed traces, gives the cheapest path; a branch ends on its trunk's trace, one layer through the branch point (a via goes on the branch). "fixed" = pad to pad as planned before routing (the shortest straight-line tree), no branch points. |
| `steiner` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Topological core: free Steiner points on a 2 mm grid in the open areas of the board, as extra vertices of the projection (the triangulation the topology is planned on) and as candidate branch points: a trace of a multi-pin net may then split at a free point on another trace of its net (a Y) instead of joining at a pad. false (default) = the projection is built from the fixed items only (pads, vias, keepouts, copper graphics, the board outline), once per run, as in TopoR; a net's tree joins pad to pad or through a pad already on a trace of its net (both the pad-to-pad chain and the Y are correct routing; the Y can be shorter, the grid makes the projection larger and the run slower). Only with net_tree = "free" does the grid add branch points. |
| `length` | str | `"taut"` |  | even\|taut | Topological core: how the path search prices a trace's length while it plans the topology. "taut" (default) = the shortest path through the trace's corridor of triangles that keeps the clearances: to the pads and the board edge at the ends of every crossed edge of the triangulation and to the traces already crossing it there (TopoR's initial routing takes "the shortest path on the triangulation with the clearances needed", Polubasov 2010); this works the same with and without the Steiner grid (steiner). "even" (the default before M0, the behaviour before 4.3) = between evenly spaced points on each crossed edge: a good estimate only on short edges, so without the Steiner grid (long edges) it overrates straight paths and plans detours (measured 4.2: wiccon-2023 GPIO0 4.45 x its straight length). |
| `crossing_vias` | str | `"crossing"` |  | crossing\|via | Topological core: how the search prices a crossing of two nets. "crossing" (default) = the crossing factor ([factors] crossing, 20 mm: TopoR takes a 13-20 mm detour rather than a via pair) stands for the layer change the layer assignment makes; only a crossing that no layer assignment can separate (both traces held to the same single layer where they cross, e.g. over another net's pad on the other side) is priced as a violation (the overflow factor). "via" = also price, with the via factor, the via that a crossing of two traces held to the same layer implies, and keep the trace on the other layer after it (measured D6b: on qmtech 16 fewer connections, more vias; on a 2-layer badge the same). |
| `branch_relocate` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Topological core, net_tree = "free": the plan moves each branch point (T junction) of a net to where its three arms are shortest together: the Steiner (Fermat) point, where they meet at 120 degrees, when every angle of the three arm ends is below 120 degrees; when the two arms at a pad meet at less than 120 degrees the junction is pulled out of the pad to that point; when an angle at a pad is 120 degrees or more the junction goes into that pad (Popov & Popov 2013; TopoR FreeStyle "move T-points"). With [draw] style = "octilinear" the point is the one of least octilinear length instead (the legs run at 0 / 45 / 90 degrees, where the 120 degree point is not the shortest). A move is kept only where the new arms keep their clearances (a move their clearance stops part way goes as far as they keep it; the report counts these). Needs [search] length = "taut" (the point is computed on the plan's wire paths; skipped with a warning otherwise). |
| `junction_pad_mm` | float | `0.0` | mm | 0 .. 20 | Topological core, net_tree = "free": a branch point on a trace closer than this to a pad of the copper it joins is not used; the pad itself is the junction (the trace runs through the pad centre) instead of a T next to it. 0 = no such distance (default): the junction_angle and branch factors decide between a T next to a pad and the pad itself on price. |
| `fuse_branches` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core, net_tree = "free": after the drawing, a trace that leaves a branch point or a pad right beside another trace of its net leaves that trace's copper where the two part instead: one copper and a T there, no two parallel traces (TopoR moves T-points the same way in its post-optimisation). Done only where it is shorter, the junction_angle factor included, and the new track keeps every clearance. |
| `fuse_pour_check` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core, board with copper pours: the steps after the drawing that move copper (fuse_branches and, with style = octilinear, the polish that redraws the segments not at 0/45/90 degrees as an elbow or Z) are judged by the pour stitching too. The copper with and without their moves is stitched; when the moved copper leaves more pour pieces cut off (each one is an unconnected item in KiCad's DRC after a zone refill), the moves nearest those pieces are undone, and all of them when that is not enough. Off: these steps are judged by length and clearance only. Costs two or more stitching passes (about 1.5 s each on a 4-layer board with 600 connections). |
| `fuse_pour_rounds` | int | `2` |  | 0 .. 10 | Topological core, fuse_pour_check on: how many times the check undoes the moves nearest the pour pieces only the moved copper leaves cut off and stitches again, before it undoes every move of the fuse and the polish. 0 = undo every move at once when the moved copper leaves more pieces cut off. |
| `margin_um` | float | `0` | µm | 0 .. 1000 | Safety margin added to every clearance during search and drawing; 0 = exactly the design rule (KiCad DRC accepts copper at exactly the clearance, and the routed copper is checked with the exact rule). Raise it only for headroom against later manual edits. |
| `neck_to_pad` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Necking: an exit stub may be narrower than the net's track width (down to KiCad's minimum track width or the net's custom-rule minimum) where the full width does not fit out of the pad; the rest of the trace keeps its width. The run report lists every necked stub. KiCad: KiCad → File → Board Setup → Design Rules → Constraints → Minimum track width (and custom rules: track_width min). |
| `neck_from_pad` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core, width in the plan: where a trace's net width does not fit a passage (a bottleneck, or the way out of a fine-pitch pad), the planner narrows it down to the minimum width, from the nearest pad of the connection up to that passage (a neck starts at the footprint and may reach further back to make room for other traces; never a narrow stretch in the middle of a full-width trace). Off: only the bottleneck passages themselves are narrowed. Every necked stretch is a warning in the report and costs the necking factor. KiCad: KiCad → File → Board Setup → Design Rules → Constraints → Minimum track width (and custom rules: track_width min). |
| `pad_exit_stubs` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Topological core, pad exits (experimental, off by default): where a trace leaves a fine-pitch pad (a long, narrow SMD pad with another net's copper beside it closer than the trace could pass, e.g. a QFP or SSOP pin row), its way out is decided before the topology is planned: straight out of the pad's tip that faces the trace's other end, along the pad's long axis, until the trace can turn without coming closer than the clearance to the neighbouring pins (the clearance plus the track width past the tip). That stub is a fixed item like a pad: other traces are planned round its end instead of across the pin's way out, and the room between its end and the neighbouring pins is a cut the capacity model prices ([capacity] model). A stub that would break a clearance is left out (the trace then leaves the pad as without the option). The tip is chosen from the straight line to the trace's other end, not yet by the planner: where the planner takes the trace out of the other tip (for example round the end pin of the row, because going the direct way would cross a neighbour's trace), the stub only takes room from the other traces, and the drawing may then pass a neighbouring pin's tip too closely (clearance violations on QFP/SSOP inner fan-outs). On dense fine-pitch boards it removes many pad-exit violations; on boards with traces that leave pins through the inner tip it can add some. Off (default): the exits are left to the plan and the drawing (the behaviour before 5.10). |
| `drawing_feedback` | str | `"auto"` |  | auto\|on\|off | Topological core: a connection whose copper the drawing step could not fit (a clearance to a pad or to a trace drawn earlier would be violated) is drawn first and the traces that block its corridor are drawn again around it, once per connection, instead of being reported failed at once; with [optimize] loop = "cycles" the room the drawing found too narrow also feeds into the next cycle's plan. "auto" (default) = on with loop = "cycles" (the behaviour before M0), off with loop = "topor": TopoR computes the copper once from the topology (Polubasov 2010, introduction: the exact shape of the wires and the positions of the vias are computed on the metric stage), so a connection the drawing cannot fit is reported, not redrawn around others; "on" / "off" (or true / false) force it. With loop = "topor" nothing of the drawing reaches the plan in any setting (no room hints, M2); "on" there has no effect either (M6, 2026-11-18: the one drawing never redraws the traces that block a connection it could not fit; the run warns that the setting is ignored): only loop = "cycles" reads it. |
| `feedback_max_rip` | int | `8` |  | 0 .. 100 | Work cap: most already drawn traces one such feedback round may take out and draw again (a larger value rescues more connections and costs more runtime). Whether they are taken out at all is a graded price, not this count: the reroute factor's price per blocking trace (more for one redrawn before in the same round) against the violation factor's price of drawing the rejected connection through them; the cheapest rescues go first. |
| `reroute_rounds` | int | `6` |  | 0 .. 50 | Topological core: most rounds of negotiated rip-up-and-reroute. After the layers are assigned, the connections that run through a passage holding more copper on one layer than fits are taken out and routed again, with a growing price (the congestion factor) on the passages that were over-full, until none is over-full or a round brings no gain; the best round is kept. 0 = off. With [optimize] loop = "topor" these rounds run only when [optimize] preloop_p4 = true (the default; false: the loop's history and layering escapes do their work). |
| `neck_max_mm` | float | `0.0` | mm | 0 .. 100 | Longest necked stub; 0 = twice the pad's long side. |
| `dangling_ends` | str | `"continue"` |  | continue\|fixed\|drop | What to do with an existing track that ends at nothing (a hand-started trace): continue = the new copper leaves its end along the same direction (smooth, same width and layer); fixed = the end stays a fixed point and the new copper may leave at an angle; drop = remove that track and route from the pad. Known gap (continue): when another pad or via of the same hand copper is nearer the trace's other end, the trace starts there and the hand track stays dangling (KiCad's DRC then reports the dangling track). *Since 0.5.0.* |
| `dangling_lead_mm` | float | `0.0` | mm | 0 .. 20 | Topological core, dangling_ends = "continue": length of the lead that continues a dangling end straight along its direction (planned before the topology, at the hand track's width, shortened to the room ahead; where nothing fits the end is a plain terminal and the report notes it). After the lead the trace may turn; the dangling_turn factor (opt-in) prices the angle off the direction. 0 = one pitch (the connection's width + clearance). *Since 0.5.0.* |
| `dangling_lead_via` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core, dangling_ends = "continue": where the trace changes layer right at the end of a dangling end's lead (dangling_lead_mm), the lead ends at that via, placed where it fits on the lead with every clearance, KiCad's hole clearance (Board Setup → Design Rules → Constraints → Minimum hole clearance) and the board edge clearance: the netclass via (or a custom via rule) first, even if the lead ends a little shorter; a smaller pre-defined via (Board Setup → Design Rules → Pre-defined Sizes) only where the netclass via fits nowhere on the lead and its drill carries the trace (π × drill ≥ trace width). A lead the trace leaves on its own layer keeps its full length. false = the via goes where the plan put it and the lead is only checked for the track. *Since 0.5.0.* |
| `dangling_lead_choice` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Topological core, dangling_ends = "continue": the lead of a dangling end (dangling_lead_mm) becomes a choice of the plan: the trace may also start at the hand end itself or at 1/3 or 2/3 of the lead, each leaving along the hand track's direction, and the cheapest start wins: the length from it plus the turn there, priced by the dangling_turn factor in [factors] weight (with this option on its default is 4 instead of 0; a weight set there wins; the lead up to the start is free, as the fixed lead is). A lead that points past its target gets shorter (or none); the drawing draws it only up to the chosen point. The unused part of the lead still keeps other nets away in the plan. false (default) = the trace always starts at the lead's end. *Since 0.5.0.* |

## `[optimize]`

Topological core: how a run iterates (by default TopoR's loop on the topology: the initial routing once, then rip-up and reroute, layer re-optimisation and an archive of variants, the pick drawn once; best of N seeded runs), its safety caps (work caps, so a run is reproducible), and which result it keeps.

| Key | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rounds` | int | `30` |  | 1 .. 1000 | Topological core: safety cap on whole-route cycles per run (the first one included). A run does not stop at a fixed count: like TopoR it keeps iterating (every cycle routes again with the passages the drawing found too small lowered and with freshly fluctuated weights, and offers its result variants) until its routes are stable (see stable_window), the user presses OK / Cancel, or run.timeout_s fires; this cap only ends a run that never settles. A work cap, not a time cap: the same board and settings give the same result on any machine, loaded or not, and with any thread count. |
| `initial` | str | `"once"` |  | per_cycle\|once | Topological core: when the initial routing (every connection laid one at a time: net priority tier first (1 = first), then widest, then shortest) runs. "once" (default) = once per run, in its first cycle, as in TopoR: double crossings are removed after every trace (not once after all) and the traces that took part in a removal are laid anew, the new lay kept only when its price (length and crossings) is lower, and every trace is placed: a trace with no legal topological path still goes through, at the very high price of the violation factor ([factors] violation), and so does a crossing that no layer assignment can separate (a crossing on one layer); the later cycles start from the plan of the cycle before and improve it (rip-up and reroute, crossing rules) instead of laying everything again. A crossing on one layer that survives into the final copper is reported as a CRITICAL warning (traces X and Y cross on layer L), never as a dropped trace; so is a drawn trace whose copper overlaps a pad, via, track or no-tracks rule area of another net (trace X runs through ... on layer L). "per_cycle" (the default before M0, the behaviour before 4.3) = every cycle lays all traces again from scratch. With loop = "topor" the initial routing always runs once. |
| `loop` | str | `"topor"` |  | cycles\|topor | Topological core: how a run iterates. "cycles" (the default before M0, the behaviour before 5.1) = whole-route cycles: every cycle plans the topology and draws it, and what the drawing found too narrow feeds into the next cycle's plan ([search] drawing_feedback). "topor" (default) = TopoR's loop (Polubasov 2010): the initial routing runs once (as initial = "once"), then the run iterates on the topology only, nothing drawn inside the loop: every cycle takes the traces out one at a time and lays them again where that is cheaper, each trace with its own oscillating weights; then the layers are assigned again (a random one of the layerings with the same number of vias), the traces whose vias rose are laid again, the label moves move stretches to the other layer (floating up) and the crossing rules run. Each cycle's plan is judged by its predicted violations (cuts too narrow for what passes them, including the gap between a pad and the board edge; crossings no layer assignment separates; a trace planned through a pad or other copper of another net), vias, length and shrinkages and kept in an archive of variants (as the drawn ones were); every run offers its plans to one variant table shared by all runs, and from time to time a run whose descent no longer gains goes on from a row of that table picked at random (restart; seeded, so the same settings give the same result). The loop ends when the plan is stable (loop_stable_window, stable_gain_pct; runs without the progress dialog only: with the dialog it goes on after "Routes stable" until your OK), at rounds cycles, or at loop_time_share of the time left; the four bests of the variant table (TopoR 6.3 manual pp. 72-73: overall = fewest errors, then length + mm_per_via per via; fewest errors; shortest and least vias among the rows with the fewest errors; [drawing] candidates of them) are drawn, each distinct row once, and compared as drawn; [optimize] pick says which of them goes to the board. An OK / Cancel during the loop ends the loop and still draws the overall best. Use it with [search] length = "taut" (the default; the loop compares lengths of plans). |
| `loop_restart` | int | `2` |  | 0 .. 1000 | Topological core, loop = "topor", restart = stall and hybrid: cycles in which the picked variant did not get better after which the loop goes on from an archived variant picked at random (seeded; TopoR "periodically stops working on the current variant and picks one from the table at random", Polubasov 2010). 0 = never restart (the loop always goes on from where the last cycle ended). |
| `loop_stable_window` | int | `8` |  | 1 .. 1000 | Topological core, loop = "topor": the loop's plan is stable when its picked variant gained less than stable_gain_pct % over this many loop cycles: runs without the progress dialog (harness, MCP) end the loop there (plus stable_patience); with the dialog it shows "Routes stable", the Cancel button turns into OK and the loop keeps iterating until you press it (or the rounds safety cap / run.timeout_s). A loop cycle draws nothing and is cheap, so this window is longer than stable_window (the drawn cycles of loop = "cycles"). With restart = periodic (default) stable is the variant table's: its four bests gained nothing over at least this many cycles and, since their last gain, two period checks found a descent free (it restarted, or had no other row to go to). A work cap like rounds: the same settings give the same result on any machine. |
| `loop_via_start` | float | `0.5` |  | 0 .. 10 | Topological core, loop = "topor": weight of the via factors (via, crossing: a crossing of two nets stands for the via the layer assignment makes) at the start of every cycle's sweep over the traces, relative to their [factors] weight. With loop_via_end above it, each cycle first shortens the traces and later removes vias (TopoR: "at the start of a cycle more attention goes to the total length, at its end to the number of vias", Luzin & Polubasov 2006). The weight changes smoothly from start to end; 1 and 1 = no emphasis. |
| `loop_via_end` | float | `1.5` |  | 0 .. 10 | Topological core, loop = "topor": weight of the via factors at the end of every cycle's sweep (see loop_via_start); the traces whose vias rose in the layer assignment are laid again at this weight. |
| `loop_time_share` | float | `0.5` |  | 0.05 .. 1 | Topological core, loop = "topor": the share of the time left (run.timeout_s) that the loop may use at most; the rest is kept for the one drawing. An emergency stop like the time limit (the loop normally ends when its plan is stable); when it fires the result says so. |
| `refine_lanes` | int | `"auto"` |  | 1 .. 256 | Topological core: how many lanes (threads) evaluate the layer refinement's candidate moves at once (the label moves that take traces off over-full edges, in the layer assignment of every cycle). The lanes take the moves in the order one lane tries them and the first move that lowers the price is kept, so every lane count keeps the same moves in the same order: the plan and the copper do not depend on it, only the time does. auto (default) = one lane plus the engine's compute slots no run uses at that moment (with [optimize] loop = "topor": runs fewer than the engine's threads, or runs waiting for the others at the end of their loop; with loop = "cycles" one lane); a number = that many lanes, whatever else runs (more lanes than free threads only wait for each other). 1 = the serial refinement on one thread. |
| `measure_reuse` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core: the plan's measure (its predicted violations, which the TopoR loop's moves pay and the variants are judged by) takes the capacity model the layer refinement ended with (true, default: faster, the model is not built twice) instead of building it again from the final layers (false: the measure before par-refine). The two can differ slightly (the refinement's model keeps the via positions of the order its moves came in), so a plan can change. With [capacity] model = "cuts", or when the layers change after the refinement (the more-layer junction fix-up, the P4 label moves), the model is built again either way. |
| `loop_judge` | str | `"local"` |  | local\|global | Topological core, loop = "topor": how a loop move (a trace laid again, a via pair moved) is judged. "local" (default) = the moved traces and the traces they cross get their layers again, every other trace keeps its layers, and the move pays for what changes on the edges these traces pass (predicted violations, vias); the whole board gets its layers again once per cycle (the layer re-optimisation). Faster on big boards, the work per move grows with the move, not the board. "global" = every move assigns the layers of the whole board again (the earlier behaviour; slower on big boards). With [capacity] model = "cuts" every move is judged globally. |
| `loop_shadow` | int | `0` |  | 0 .. 1000000 | Topological core, diagnostic (loop_judge = "local"): every k-th move judged locally is also judged by the whole board and the two judgements are compared in the loop's report line (how often they keep alike, how far apart the predicted violations, vias and unlayerable crossings are). The local judgement is still the one used. 0 = off (default, no cost). |
| `local_depth` | int | `1` |  | 1 .. 8 | Topological core, loop_judge = "local": how many rings of crossing traces round a moved trace get their layers again with it. 1 (default) = the traces it crosses before and after the move; 2 = also the traces those cross (more exact, slower). |
| `oscillation` | str | `"cooling"` |  | bounded\|cooling | Topological core, loop = "topor" (TW5): how the factor weights of the loop's reroutes oscillate. "bounded" = each trace gets its own amplitude between osc_amp_min and osc_amp_max, larger the further the trace is from its straight line, the more crowded the cuts it passes and the more of its tries failed; the same in every cycle (no cooling), and the violation price of a reroute oscillates with the rest (TopoR: the coefficients are chosen per trace by the quality of its path and its surroundings and oscillate within limits, Polubasov 2010). The variant table always uses fixed weights. "cooling" (default) = the width narrows by fluctuation_narrowing per cycle and reheats when stuck (before TW5). Off by default (TW5 is under evaluation: qmtech is worse at 16 cycles, analysed per connection first). |
| `osc_amp_min` | float | `0.1` |  | 0 .. 0.9 | Topological core, oscillation = "bounded": the amplitude of a trace on a straight, uncrowded path whose tries keep gaining (the weights move within +-10 % at 0.1). |
| `osc_amp_max` | float | `0.4` |  | 0 .. 0.9 | Topological core, oscillation = "bounded": the amplitude a trace approaches the worse its path and surroundings are (never above; at least osc_amp_min). |
| `escape` | str | `"ties"` |  | layering\|ties | Topological core, loop = "topor" (TW5): the layer re-optimisation as an escape from local optima. "layering" = during the cycle's sweep the whole board gets a random layering among those with the fewest vias (a random walk over the equal-via layerings, escape_walk), as often as escape_share of the loop's work allows; it is taken as it comes (escape_take) and the traces whose via count rose are laid again first (TopoR: "the layering is chosen at random"; the gain comes from "a radical change of the topological situation", Polubasov 2010). "ties" (default) = one re-optimisation per cycle with random ties only (before TW5). Off by default (TW5 is under evaluation: qmtech is worse at 16 cycles, analysed per connection first). |
| `escape_walk` | int | `4` |  | 0 .. 1000 | Topological core, escape = "layering": tries per crossing of the random walk over the layerings with the fewest vias (more = a layering further from the present one; 0 = the solver's own optimum with random ties). |
| `escape_share` | float | `0.35` |  | 0.01 .. 0.5 | Topological core, escape = "layering": the largest share of the loop's work the layering escapes may take (at most 0.5: an escape never comes sooner than its own last duration, TopoR). Counted in work units, never the clock, so the result does not depend on the machine or its load. |
| `escape_kappa` | float | `0.07` |  | 0 .. 1000 | Topological core, escape = "layering" (tuning): the work units of one whole-board layering per trace, against a reroute's units per trace it lays out again (deterministic, never the clock; 0.07 measured: a reroute's path search makes it about 14 times dearer per trace than a layering). |
| `escape_take` | str | `"not_worse"` |  | always\|not_worse | Topological core, loop = "topor" (TW5): the whole-board moves (layering escape, floating up, crossing passes). "always" = taken as they come; the variant table keeps the best variants, so a worse state is a step on the way, never the result. "not_worse" (default) = each is undone when the board's evaluation rises (before TW5). Off by default (TW5 is under evaluation: qmtech is worse at 16 cycles, analysed per connection first). |
| `relay_count_fade` | float | `1.0` |  | 0 .. 1 | Topological core, loop = "topor" (TW5): the price of laying a trace again once more ([factors] reroute, per earlier reroute) counts its reroutes fading by this per cycle, so a trace that moves back and forth gets dearer but no trace is frozen for the rest of a long run. 1 (default) = the count never fades (before TW5); 0.8 with the other TW5 options. Off by default (TW5 is under evaluation: qmtech is worse at 16 cycles, analysed per connection first). |
| `loop_history` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Topological core, loop = "topor" (TW5): an edge that stays over-full gets a history price inside the loop ([factors] congestion per pass), growing while it stays over-full and fading by loop_history_fade per layering, so traces with another way leave it (PathFinder, McMurchie & Ebeling 1995). false (default) = only the history of the rounds before the loop. Off by default (TW5 is under evaluation: qmtech is worse at 16 cycles, analysed per connection first). |
| `loop_history_fade` | float | `0.8` |  | 0 .. 0.99 | Topological core, loop_history: the factor the loop history fades by per update (the history stays below 1 / (1 - fade): 5 at 0.8). |
| `float_wire` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Topological core, loop = "topor", loop_judge = "local" (TW5): floating up per trace: after a trace's reroute was not kept, the layers of the trace and of the traces it crosses are chosen again (tried more often the worse the trace's path and surroundings), kept when that is cheaper (TopoR "floating up", Polubasov 2010). Off by default (TW5 is under evaluation: qmtech is worse at 16 cycles, analysed per connection first). |
| `preloop_p4` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core, loop = "topor" (TW5): run the negotiated rip-up rounds ([search] reroute_rounds) before the loop. false = the loop does their work (its history on over-full edges and the layering escapes); true (default) = before TW5. Off by default (TW5 is under evaluation: qmtech is worse at 16 cycles, analysed per connection first). |
| `loop_p4` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Topological core, loop = "topor" (TW5): one negotiated rip-up round per cycle inside the loop, after the sweep: the traces of the passages that stay over-full (and of vias without a site) are taken out together and routed again, so one of them can make room for the others (a detour or two vias) where moving one trace at a time cannot. Kept like the loop's other whole-board moves ([optimize] escape_take: "not_worse" undoes a round that makes the board worse, "always" keeps it and the variant table keeps the bests); a round in which a trace finds no path is undone. Its work is bounded by [optimize] escape_share of the loop's work; with escape = "layering" on too, the escapes and the rounds get half of it each (a shared budget starved the rounds) and turns the loop's history on over-full passages on (as [optimize] loop_history). With preloop_p4 = false it does the pre-loop rounds' work inside the loop. false (default) = before TW5 (f). Off by default until measured. |
| `escape_offer` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core, loop = "topor" (TW5): the board as a layering escape ([optimize] escape = "layering") or an in-loop rip-up round ([optimize] loop_p4) left it goes to the variant table right away, before the rest of the cycle changes it, so a best variant reached there is kept (TopoR: the table keeps the variants that are best by some criterion). A state the table already holds an equal or better variant for is not copied. Acts only with those options on. true (default); false = the table gets the board only at the end of each cycle. |
| `free_wire_cross` | float | `1.0` |  | 0 .. 1 | Topological core, loop = "topor" (TW5): what crossing a trace that crosses nothing else costs in the loop's reroutes, as a share a of the crossing price; a trace with k crossings of its own costs a + (1 - a) k/(1 + k), so the price grows smoothly back to the full one. Below 1 such a trace also counts as free to take any layer its own pads allow (it is drawn on the bottom layer while nothing crosses it). A layering separates a crossing with a free trace without a via, so TopoR does not count it (Polubasov 2010, fig. 4). 1 (default) = every crossing at the full price, a trace without crossings held to the bottom layer (before TW5). Off by default until measured. |
| `loop_crossing` | float | `0.25` |  | 0 .. 1 | Topological core, loop = "topor": share of the crossing factor's weight ([factors] crossing) that a crossing of two nets keeps in the loop's reroutes. The loop lays each trace into the present layering: a crossing the trace can take on another layer than the crossed stretch costs this share only, a crossing that forces the trace to change layer costs the via (and the via back, where it has to return to its pad's layer) at the via weight on top (TopoR: before the optimisation every stretch gets a layer, and a crossing of a stretch with a via is penalised, Polubasov 2010). 1 = the full crossing price on top of the vias; 0 = only the vias. |
| `max_ripped` | int | `5000` |  | 0 .. 1000000 | Topological core: most connections one whole-route round may take out and route again (negotiated rip-up-and-reroute, drawing feedback and the P4 moves together). A work cap (see rounds). |
| `max_expansions` | int | `2000000` |  | 1000 .. 1000000000 | Topological core: search cap per connection (expanded search nodes); the one retry of a connection that found no path uses four times this. A work cap (see rounds): a connection that needs more is reported as failed. |
| `objective` | str | `"length_vias"` |  | length_vias\|area | Topological core: how the result variants are judged. Every whole-route round gives two variants (as drawn, and after the via reduction); the archive keeps every variant no other beats on all four TopoR criteria (errors = connections not routed, vias, total length, shrinkages = necked stretches). length_vias = fewest errors first, then by [optimize] pick (default: fewest vias, then the shortest length; errors_weighted: the least length + mm_per_via x vias); area = fewest errors first, then the least occupied area (a trace counts length x (width + clearance), a via its pad-plus-clearance disc on every layer). The run report lists the variant table and marks the pick; the picked variant goes to KiCad. |
| `pick` | str | `"best"` |  | best\|errors\|shortest\|vias\|errors_weighted\|errors_vias_length | Topological core: the order of the final choice and which of the four bests goes to KiCad, for objective = length_vias (TW3, user decision D5 2026-11-18). best (default) = the overall best at 100 % drawn: fewest errors (connections left open or with a rule violation in their copper, pour pieces cut off included), fewest connections with a short among equals (pick_shorts), then the least total length + mm_per_via x vias (TopoR 6.3 manual pp. 72-73: violations first, then length; 25 mm/via), then fewest shrinkages; best_penalty adds the violation price. errors = the drawn row with the fewest errors and the least violation price (how deep and long its violations are); shortest / vias = the drawn row with the shortest length / the fewest vias among those with the fewest errors (the variant table's four bests, [drawing] candidates). errors_weighted = best with the violation price (the order before 2026-11-10); errors_vias_length = fewest errors, shorts, open connections, vias, then length (the default 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-18). The search itself (rip-up rounds, factors, mm_per_via as a price) does not change. objective = area ignores it. KiCad's own DRC runs once on the result handed back; it is not used to rank. |
| `best_penalty` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Topological core, pick = best (TW3): add the graded violation price (the violation factor's price of how deep and long the violations are, in mm at the violation weight) to the overall best's length + mm_per_via x vias. Off (default) = the user's order D5: fewest errors, then length + mm_per_via x vias. On = the same order as errors_weighted. |
| `restart` | str | `"hybrid"` |  | hybrid\|periodic\|stall\|off | Topological core, loop = "topor" (TW3): how a run's descent goes on from the one variant table all runs share. hybrid (default) = a stall (loop_restart cycles in which the run's own pick did not get better, no cycle floor) restarts the run from a row of the table drawn at random (seeded), never its own state, and the periodic check below stays as the backstop. periodic = TopoR's "periodically stops working on the current variant and picks one from the table at random" (Polubasov 2010): every restart_relays re-lays (the loop's time, counted in work so the same settings give the same result on any machine; at least restart_min_cycles cycles) a run looks at the table; when its descent is free (it gave the table no new row since the last look, or it is in the same state as a lower run) it goes on from a row drawn at random (seeded), worse rows too, never its own state; a descent that still gains is never cut. Without the progress dialog the loop ends at stable only when the table's four bests gained nothing over at least loop_stable_window cycles and, since their last gain, two period checks found a descent free (restarted, or no other row to go to). With the dialog (hybrid and periodic) rounds is not a cap: OK, Cancel and the time limit end the loop. stall = after loop_restart cycles without a better own pick (the rule before 2026-11-18); off = never restart; with stall and off the dialog's loop still ends at rounds, as before TW3. |
| `restart_relays` | int | `800` |  | 1 .. 10000000 | Topological core, restart = hybrid / periodic: the period between two looks at the variant table, in re-lays tried (one trace taken out and laid again; the loop's unit of time): 800 is about 9 cycles on esp-rust-board (~90 re-lays a cycle), 14 on wiccon and the restart_min_cycles floor on qmtech (~320 a cycle). A work count, not seconds: the same settings give the same result on any machine and thread count. |
| `restart_min_cycles` | int | `8` |  | 1 .. 1000 | Topological core, restart = hybrid / periodic: a period is never shorter than this many loop cycles (a descent gets at least this many cycles before it may be replaced). |
| `loop_relays` | int | `0` |  | 0 .. 1000000000 | Topological core, loop = "topor" (TW3): each run's loop ends after this many re-lays (one trace taken out and laid again; the loop's work clock, so the same settings give the same result on any machine). 0 = no budget (the default; rounds, stable, OK / Cancel and the time limit end the loop). For comparisons at an equal amount of loop work. A run ended by it reports the stop reason "re-lay budget" (a work cap like rounds, which reports "round cap"). |
| `pick_shorts` | bool | `true` |  | true\|false | Topological core: connections with a short (their copper overlaps copper of another net: a track over another net's track, pad or via, or two nets crossing on one layer; KiCad DRC shorting_items / tracks_crossing, and the track KiCad's Cleanup removes) are a criterion of their own in every choice between results: right after the errors (they are errors already, so not counted twice), before the open connections, the vias and the length. So of two results with the same number of errors the one with fewer shorts wins, even when it leaves a connection open or is longer: a short fails the board in DRC, an open is visible and stays the router's to finish. It applies to the final pick (archive variants and seeded runs), to the TopoR loop's choice of the plan it draws (the predicted shorts: crossings no layer assignment separates and traces planned through copper of another net) and to the rip-up rounds' plan score (per-edge capacity model). It also feeds the stable meter (a short fewer at the same error count is a gain, like a completion), and the meter drives the reheat schedule and the stable / finish stop, so the option changes which rounds a run makes, not only how ties are broken in the final pick. Predicted traces through a no-tracks rule area stay violations but are no shorts (KiCad reports them as rule-area violations). false = shorts counted only as errors, as before 2026-11-12; the archive's cap pruning keeps the picked variant either way (a fix made with this option, not switched by it). |
| `short_weight` | float | `1.0` |  | 1 .. 100 | Topological core (with pick_shorts): k, how many errors a connection with a short counts in every choice between results. The ranked error count is errors + (k - 1) x shorts: at k = 1 (default) a short is one error like any other, as TopoR's variant table counts violations (6.3 manual p. 72), and the fewer shorts only decide between results with the same error count (the order since 2026-11-12). A larger k is graded, not a hard rule: a result with fewer shorts wins over one with up to (k - 1) more other errors per short removed (a short fails the board in KiCad's DRC and Cleanup removes the track; an open or a clearance violation is visible and fixable by hand). Applies wherever pick_shorts does (final pick, Pareto pruning, stable meter, TopoR loop plan pick, rip-up rounds' plan score). Values below 1 count as 1. No larger default has been measured yet: that needs a run that writes the alternative variants and checks each in KiCad. |
| `mm_per_via` | float | `25.0` | mm | 0 .. 1000 | Via price in mm of trace per via (TopoR: good results at 25 mm/via): the price the rip-up-and-reroute uses to pick its best round and that the archive uses to prune variants when it is over its cap; also the final pick when pick = errors_weighted (objective = length_vias). |
| `variants` | int | `8` |  | 1 .. 100 | Most result variants the archive keeps (population size); the best variant on each criterion (fewest errors, shortest, fewest vias, fewest shrinkages, fewest warnings) is always kept on top. |
| `moves` | bool | `false` |  | true\|false | Topological core: after the rip-up-and-reroute, a descent of local moves, each kept only when it lowers the price of the social factors ([factors]): reroute a connection, connect it to another pad of its net, put it next to a parallel trace of its net, slide a crossing along a shared channel, reroute two crossing connections in the other order, remove double crossings; then on the layers: swap the layers of a crossing, shift a via along its trace, lift a stretch onto another layer. The descent is kept only when the board objective after the layer assignment improves. Off by default: measured on the gate boards it routed 6 more connections on tanmatsu but 7 fewer on hackerhotel2027 and 1 fewer on bornhack2026 (the drawing does not always follow the topological objective); try it per board. |
| `max_moves` | int | `400` |  | 0 .. 1000000 | Most move evaluations of that descent per whole-route round (the layer moves have the same cap). A work cap (see rounds). |
| `fluctuation` | float | `0.2` |  | 0 .. 0.9 | Fluctuation schedule, start width: in every cycle each factor weight is multiplied by a seeded random factor between 1 - width and 1 + width (search, rip-up-and-reroute and descent), so the search leaves local optima (TopoR's fluctuating coefficients). The width starts here, narrows every cycle (fluctuation_narrowing) and is widened again when the run is stuck (fluctuation_stuck, fluctuation_reheat): annealing with reheating. The first cycle of the first run always uses the plain weights. The seed is fixed, so runs stay reproducible; 0 = fixed weights throughout. |
| `fluctuation_narrowing` | float | `0.7` |  | 0 .. 1 | Fluctuation schedule: the width is multiplied by this after every cycle (1 = constant width, smaller = narrows faster). |
| `fluctuation_stuck` | int | `2` |  | 0 .. 100 | Fluctuation schedule: after this many cycles without a better result while connections are still not complete, the width is set back to fluctuation_reheat and narrows again from there; 0 = never widen again. |
